subject: crab-code
title: 7-level usage-percentage compaction ladder with no-LLM tiers first and a session circuit breaker
one_why: Snip(no-LLM)->Microcompact->Summarize->Hybrid->Truncate by usage band, image-block strip before any compaction on prompt-too-long, and 3-failure circuit breaker stop the summarize-everything reflex; finer-grained than codex's 3 tiers -- but the Microcompact level self-declares as a Claude Code port (micro_compact.rs:8), so port the ladder shape as concept only.

subject: crab-code
title: Swap to a larger-context variant of the same model at 75% before resorting to compaction
one_why: Ordered warn/upgrade/compact thresholds make 'model family with 200k and 1M variants' a capacity lever that preserves full history where every other subject jumps straight to lossy summarization; crab-original, no license encumbrance, emits a user-visible ContextUpgraded event.

subject: crab-code
title: Deny-wins-as-security-boundary invariant, cross-layer tested, plus quote-aware per-segment deny for chained bash
one_why: The deny-before-allow ordering is documented as a security boundary and pinned by a dedicated spec across config layers (user-allow vs project-deny), and `echo ok && rm -rf x` is split quote-aware so each segment is re-matched -- the whole-command-match hole most allow/deny lists have; DontAsk's final ask->deny pass blocks prompt leakage on non-interactive runs.

subject: crab-code
title: Transform-style prepare_command with per-platform backends: Landlock fail-closed, seatbelt PATH-hijack-hardened, Windows honestly fail-open
one_why: Sandboxing as a command transformation (raw argv + policy in, confined Command out) keeps the sandbox crate out of every tool; NotEnforced kernel => spawn error not silent passthrough, /usr/bin/sandbox-exec hardcoded, and denial-hint attribution disabled on fail-open Windows so failures aren't misattributed -- but 39 sandbox tests never spawn a confined process to prove a write is refused, which is what caps safety at 7.

subject: crab-code
title: Concurrent teammate approvals coalesce into one prompt with broadcast decisions
one_why: Teammates have no terminal, so they ask through the session's handler; PermissionSyncManager lets the first asker prompt and every concurrent identical asker awaits + observes that answer -- the fix for approval-card storms in multi-agent runs, without any auto-approve side door.

subject: crab-code
title: Closed LlmBackend enum leaves no injection seam: 4,971 tests but the agent loop never runs against a scripted provider
one_why: LlmBackend is an enum over concrete clients, so query_loop's rich recovery paths (PTL retry, fallback replay, truncation escalation, orphan-tool_use backfill) are only unit-tested at the helper level; the 'E2E' suite builds a client aimed at http://localhost:0 -- codex's mock-SSE suite exists precisely to close this, and without it verification stays at 7.

subject: crab-code
title: 'Built from scratch' contradicted by per-module maps to Claude Code internal TS files
one_why: Module-level 'Maps to Claude Code's microCompact.ts / bashClassifier.ts / SkillTool / applyGrouping+CollapsedReadSearchContent' comments and a whole-table structural mapping to internal dirs (services/compact, memdir, cli.tsx) name things only visible from source-level access to proprietary Claude Code -- and this corpus already holds leaked CC snapshots (free-code); MIT license notwithstanding, treat declared-mapped modules as derivative-lineage, concepts-only for us.

subject: crab-code
title: Denial-loop tracker (3 consecutive / 20 total) instead of a generic repetition breaker
one_why: Circuit-breaker pattern applied to the failure channels that actually stall agents (permission denials, compaction failures) with warning thresholds -- cheap and actionable, but like crush there is no generic repeated-tool-call detector for benign-but-looping behavior.

subject: crab-code
title: Oversized tool outputs spill to temp files with a 2k-char in-band preview pointing Read at the full text
one_why: Per-tool max_chars budget enforced centrally in the executor rather than per-tool; soft-fail (write errors swallowed, preview still returned) keeps the tool result path unbreakable -- convergence with other subjects that discovered the same pattern.

subject: crab-code
title: /rewind via per-file path-hash version snapshots, LRU-capped at 100 per session, no git involvement
one_why: Pre-edit contents saved as {path-hash}@v{N} under the session dir, so revert works on non-git projects and never touches user git state -- lighter than cline's git-stash checkpoints, at the cost of no workspace-wide atomic rewind.

subject: crab-code
title: MCP server prompts auto-converted into namespaced skills at connect
one_why: Every prompts/get result becomes a Skill under mcp__<server>__<prompt> in the one_why registry, unifying slash-command and skill surfaces with MCP-published workflows; per-server failures skipped with logging instead of aborting registration -- clean seam between the skills crate (MCP-unaware) and the bridge.
